disease: DiGeorge / velocardiofacial syndrome -- 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (contiguous-gene microdeletion, typically the ~2.5-3 Mb LCR22A-D deletion encompassing ~40 genes incl. TBX1)
suspended_reason: The cause is a CONTIGUOUS-GENE MICRODELETION -- a heterozygous SUB-CHROMOSOMAL deletion of chromosome band 22q11.2 (most commonly the ~2.5-3 Mb LCR22A-D interval, ~85-90% of cases) that removes APPROXIMATELY 40 GENES AT ONCE (including TBX1, COMT, DGCR8, CRKL, plus microRNAs and lncRNAs) -- NOT a single-gene NUCLEAR promoter switch. The deletion arises by meiotic NON-ALLELIC HOMOLOGOUS RECOMBINATION between the flanking low-copy repeats (LCR22A-H), the same architecture that makes 22q11.2 the MOST COMMON recurrent microdeletion in humans (~1/2,000-1/4,000 live births). This opens a SIXTH held MECHANISM CLASS -- the sub-chromosomal MULTI-GENE COPY-NUMBER-VARIANT (contiguous-gene microdeletion) -- distinct from every class the kit already holds: (1) WHOLE-CHROMOSOME ANEUPLOIDY (Down = a whole extra chromosome 21, a GAIN of one entire chromosome) -- 22q11.2DS is the structural CONVERSE and a different scale: a segmental LOSS of part of one chromosome, not a whole-chromosome gain; (2) IMPRINTING (Prader-Willi / Angelman 15q11-q13, Beckwith-Wiedemann 11p15.5) -- 22q11.2DS is NOT parent-of-origin-dependent (de novo on either parental chromosome, autosomal-dominant when inherited); (3) REPEAT-DEREPRESSION (FSHD's D4Z4-DUX4); (4)-(5) the MITOCHONDRIAL GENOME (LHON / MELAS point mutations; Kearns-Sayre structural deletion). The reasons it is unreadable by a single-promoter engine are decisive. (a) ~40 GENES ARE DELETED SIMULTANEOUSLY, so there is NO SINGLE causal gene -- and therefore no single nuclear RefSeq promoter from which to emerge a gamma switch; the kit's data path resolves ONE promoter per locus, and a 40-gene contiguous deletion has no single readable promoter at all. (b) The phenotype is a CONTIGUOUS-GENE syndrome of extreme VARIABLE EXPRESSIVITY and INCOMPLETE PENETRANCE (congenital heart / conotruncal defects, thymic + parathyroid hypoplasia with immunodeficiency + hypocalcaemia, palatal anomalies, craniofacial features, neuropsychiatric risk) shaped by the COMBINED haploinsufficiency of many genes plus genetic modifiers ELSEWHERE in the genome -- a polygenic-within-the-deletion, continuous, multi-system quantity a strand-symmetric single-promoter switch cannot capture. (c) TBX1 HAPLOINSUFFICIENCY is the PRINCIPAL DOSAGE-SENSITIVE DRIVER of the major (cardiac / thymic / craniofacial) features -- and rare ISOLATED TBX1 point mutations can PHENOCOPY part of the syndrome -- but the FULL 22q11.2DS is NOT reducible to TBX1 alone (COMT, DGCR8/miRNA biogenesis, CRKL and others contribute), so even reading the TBX1 promoter would NOT emerge 'the disease': the disease is the multi-gene deletion, not one switch. Held per the author's rule -- no analyzable single-gene NUCLEAR promoter DNA -> hold. Like the other holds, suspended NOT for lack of intervention but purely on engine-readability: management is multidisciplinary and supportive (cardiac surgery, calcium/PTH and immune surveillance with thymus transplantation for complete athymia, palatal and developmental support) -- but none is a single-(nuclear)-promoter switch the engine can read. A multi-gene-CNV / dosage / modifier model is future work, not a single-switch emergence. (McDonald-McGinn 2015 Nat Rev Dis Primers 1:15071, 22q11.2 deletion syndrome; Lindsay 2001 Nature 410:97 + Merscher 2001 Cell 104:619, Tbx1 haploinsufficiency drives the DiGeorge phenotype.)
discipline: no analyzable single-gene DNA read -> held (author's rule). Disclosed, not dropped.
